title: HBM Equipment and Materials: Which Companies Supply Hanmi, Soulbrain, DISCO and Namics
content:
Korean companies hold 83% of the HBM (high-bandwidth memory) market, with SK hynix at 50% and Samsung Electronics at 33% (Counterpoint, Q2 2026, by revenue), but the equipment and materials that make HBM are split between Korea and Japan. Korea leads in thermo-compression (TC) bonders (Hanmi Semiconductor), copper-removal slurry (Soulbrain) and titanium etchant (ENF Technology), while wafer grinding and dicing equipment (DISCO) and MR-MUF material (Namics) are Japanese. Nationality was not a filter; only suppliers that could be confirmed are listed.

1. How HBM is built

HBM stacks several DRAM dies and connects the layers with tiny copper-filled holes called TSVs (through-silicon vias). The current mainstream HBM3E product is typically a 12-high stack. The sections below show which company's equipment and materials go into each step.

2. TSV etchant and copper-removal slurry

ENF Technology makes the titanium etchant that refines the film keeping copper from leaking out of the TSV, and Seoul Economic Daily reported that it displaced Japanese suppliers on HBM3E lines. Soulbrain is reported to be the world's only supplier of the slurry that removes the copper filling the TSVs; that is an October 2023 report, so the date is stated here. A separate report says Dongjin Semichem supplies HBM CMP slurry to SK hynix, but we could not confirm it is the same product.

3. Wafer thinning equipment

Equipment that grinds wafers to about half the thickness of a human hair and cuts them is reported to be led worldwide by Japan's DISCO. Some reports give its share as "70–80%" or "nearly 100%," but the agency and date of those figures are not specified, so only the ranking is given.

4. TC bonders

Hanmi Semiconductor is the world's top maker of TC bonders for HBM, with a 71.2% share based on TechInsights' cumulative Q1–Q3 2025 revenue. It has developed the tools with SK hynix since 2017 and once held around 90%, but the share fell as SK hynix began ordering from Hanwha Semitech and ASMPT too. In the same tally SEMES is second at 13.1%, followed by ASMPT at 5.6%, Yamaha Robotics at 5.6% and Hanwha Semitech at 3.2%. The bonder supplier on the Samsung Electronics side could not be confirmed. Shares change over time, so the date of each figure is stated.

5. MR-MUF material

The MR-MUF epoxy that fills gaps between stacked DRAM layers is reported by Dealsite and Business Post to be supplied 100% by Japan's Namics to SK hynix. That is 100% of SK hynix's supply, not of the world market, and Samsung Electronics uses an NCF method instead. Resonac is ranked among the top makers of NCF and TIM materials, and Tokyo Electron and Canon are named for the hybrid bonding equipment needed for HBM4. Localizing MR-MUF material is only confirmed as being attempted, not as successful.

6. The interposer linking GPU and HBM

The silicon interposer that connects the GPU and HBM side by side is made by TSMC using its CoWoS-S method; CoWoS also has CoWoS-R, which uses an RDL, and CoWoS-L, which uses an LSI bridge, so the method is specified. FC-BGA substrates from makers such as Ibiden and Shinko connect the package to the main board underneath and are a different layer from the GPU-HBM link.

7. The finished HBM

SK hynix (50%) and Samsung Electronics (33%) complete the HBM, for a combined 83%. That figure is Counterpoint's Q2 2026 revenue share, not production volume.

What could and could not be confirmed

Confirmed: Hanmi Semiconductor's TC bonder share and its date, Soulbrain's and ENF Technology's material supply, Namics' exclusive supply to SK hynix, and the HBM market shares. Not confirmed: Hanwha Semitech's TC bonder share, Duksan Hi-Metal's solder ball share (only that it is challenging Japan's Senju Metal), the bonder supplier on Samsung's side, and whether MR-MUF localization has succeeded. The information was checked against public sources through September 22, 2026, and shares may have changed since.

Quick FAQ

Does Korea make 100% of HBM?
No. SK hynix (50%) and Samsung Electronics (33%) hold 83% combined, with the rest mainly Micron of the U.S. These are revenue shares, not production volume.

Who is the world's top HBM TC bonder maker?
Hanmi Semiconductor, with 71.2% based on TechInsights' cumulative Q1–Q3 2025 revenue. It was once around 90% before SK hynix began ordering from other makers.

What does Soulbrain supply for HBM?
An October 2023 report says it is the world's only supplier of the slurry that removes copper filling the TSVs.

Does Namics' 100% supply cover the whole world?
No. It means all of SK hynix's HBM MR-MUF material is supplied by Namics; Samsung Electronics uses NCF.

Companies named are disclosed or reported suppliers; shares come from different agencies and dates and may have changed. Images are reconstructions based on public information, not an actual teardown. Sources include Counterpoint (Q2 2026 HBM share), TechInsights and Sisa Journal e (Dec 2025 TC bonder share), TheElec and Herald Business (Hanmi, Hanwha Semitech), Seoul Economic Daily (materials makers), Digital Today (Japanese suppliers), and Dealsite and Business Post (Namics supply).
